key_claims.claim: Among aspirin-treated high-risk women, the degree of first-trimester FMF-estimated risk predicts residual preterm preeclampsia risk, identifying who breaks through despite prophylaxis.
Maternal cardiovascular hemodynamic phenotype in preeclampsia correlates with antihypertensive response and long-term cardiac risk, supporting phenotype-guided management.
Women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy show persistent differences in cardiovascular and anthropometric profiles at 12 months postpartum compared to normotensive controls.
Adding EFW growth velocity to Doppler evaluation improves prediction of adverse perinatal outcomes in term SGA fetuses beyond Doppler alone.
Collaborative neurology-obstetrics care models and updated disease-modifying therapy guidance improve MS management during pregnancy and lactation.
